_comment: Task 9 (2026-07-31 bbd-part-engine) listening demo, NOT a gate -- this project does not add checksum gates for new audio paths, and this file is not wired into CMake. Deck A is ENGINE_BBD, fed the drone asset directly (input_wav) so the loop always has material circulating: FEEDBACK (LANE_MOTION) sits high so repeats build rather than decay away, and PITCH (LANE_PITCH, no lane modulation -- just the base -- so the value is exactly what the events below set) is walked across most of its travel while DETUNE (set_voice_detune) is given a real glide time, so f_clk (the target) and the CSV's a_fclk column (clock_now(), the line's actual running clock) audibly and measurably disagree for a while after each jump before the glide catches up. Deck B is silent (test_tone, LEVEL off) so only deck A's BBD is heard.

init._comment: FLOW, not STEP: a BBD deck in STEP only re-latches its clock on a fire (BbdEngine::latch_clock). FLOW's clock_flow() tracks PITCH continuously, which is what lets the walk below actually move f_clk in real time.
SOURCE -> DRIVE: a little dirt in the loop, not saturated.
SIZE -> the div ladder rung: held fixed so only PITCH is moving during the walk.
PITCH -> the clock. No lane modulation (active=false): the base IS the target, and the events below walk it directly.
MOTION -> FEEDBACK, up: repeats build instead of decaying, so the walked pitch is heard on many circulations, not just the first.
LEVEL -> MIX (spec: the wet/dry IS the level on this engine): mostly wet so the delay dominates over the dry drone.
DETUNE (menu): a real glide time, so the walk below shows f_clk chasing rather than snapping.

events._comment: PITCH walked across most of its travel: up, back down past the start, then to the middle -- three jumps, each large enough that the glide is still visibly in flight when the next one lands.
